description: Registry of every delegate appointed to the 1787 Federal Convention. Attendance and signing status follow Farrand's Records and the National Archives 'Charters of Freedom' rolls. archive_url points at the canonical public-domain compilation of the delegate's papers — typically Founders Online (founders.archives.gov), the Library of Congress, archive.org, or Project Gutenberg. The 'manifest_entry' field, where present, names the matching document_id in config/sources_manifest.json so a manifest-expansion pipeline can match delegates to their ingested source documents.

delegates.name: Abraham Baldwin
delegates.notable_role: Cast Georgia's pivotal vote on equal Senate representation, breaking the deadlock that produced the Connecticut Compromise.

delegates.name: Richard Bassett
delegates.notable_role: Among the first members of the U.S. Senate; signed the Constitution but did not speak in debate.

delegates.name: Gunning Bedford Jr.
delegates.notable_role: Forceful champion of the small states; declared the small states would 'find some foreign ally of more honor and good faith' rather than accept proportional representation in both houses.

delegates.name: John Blair
delegates.notable_role: Original Justice of the U.S. Supreme Court (1789–1796); seldom spoke at the Convention but voted consistently with Madison.

delegates.name: William Blount
delegates.notable_role: Later territorial governor and U.S. senator; first U.S. official impeached (1797).

delegates.name: David Brearley
delegates.notable_role: Chaired the Committee on Postponed Matters that framed the Electoral College compromise.

delegates.name: Jacob Broom
delegates.notable_role: Wilmington merchant and surveyor; quiet but reliable Federalist vote.

delegates.name: Pierce Butler
delegates.notable_role: Author of the Fugitive Slave Clause (Article IV, Section 2, Clause 3); later U.S. senator.

delegates.name: Daniel Carroll
delegates.notable_role: One of only two Catholic signers of the Constitution; later commissioner planning the District of Columbia.

delegates.name: George Clymer
delegates.notable_role: Signer of both the Declaration of Independence and the Constitution.

delegates.name: William Richardson Davie
delegates.notable_role: Active in Convention debates but left before signing; later secured North Carolina's belated ratification.

delegates.name: Jonathan Dayton
delegates.notable_role: At 26, the youngest signer of the Constitution; later Speaker of the House.

delegates.name: John Dickinson
delegates.notable_role: Author of 'Letters from a Farmer in Pennsylvania' (1768) and the 'Fabius' essays (1788) defending the Constitution; ill on Sept. 17 — George Read signed for him.

delegates.name: Oliver Ellsworth
delegates.notable_role: Co-architect of the Connecticut Compromise; left before signing but vigorously defended ratification as 'A Landholder' in seven essays. Later Chief Justice (1796–1800).

delegates.name: William Few
delegates.notable_role: First U.S. senator from Georgia; later autobiography is one of the few first-person accounts by a more obscure delegate.

delegates.name: Thomas Fitzsimons
delegates.notable_role: Catholic merchant; one of two Catholic signers; advocated commercial powers for Congress.

delegates.name: Benjamin Franklin
delegates.notable_role: Eldest delegate (81). Closing speech, read by James Wilson, urged signers to doubt their own infallibility — the most-quoted moment of the Convention.

delegates.name: Elbridge Gerry
delegates.notable_role: Refused to sign because the Constitution lacked a bill of rights; published 'Observations on the New Constitution' (1788). Later Vice President under Madison; namesake of 'gerrymandering'.

delegates.name: Nicholas Gilman
delegates.notable_role: Continental Army veteran; signed but spoke little in debate.

delegates.name: Nathaniel Gorham
delegates.notable_role: Chaired the Committee of the Whole. Member of the Committee of Detail that produced the first complete textual draft.

delegates.name: Alexander Hamilton
delegates.notable_role: Sole New York signer after Yates and Lansing left. Co-author (with Madison and Jay) of The Federalist; later first Secretary of the Treasury.

delegates.name: William Houston
delegates.notable_role: Continental Congress veteran; left the Convention because of failing health.

delegates.name: William Houstoun
delegates.notable_role: Distinct from N.J.'s William Houston; left before signing for Georgia.

delegates.name: Jared Ingersoll
delegates.notable_role: Federalist candidate for Vice President 1812; legal counsel in early Supreme Court cases.

delegates.name: Daniel of St. Thomas Jenifer
delegates.notable_role: Eldest signer from Maryland; consistent supporter of national-government powers.

delegates.name: William Samuel Johnson
delegates.notable_role: Chair of the Committee of Style with Morris, Hamilton, Madison, and King; later first president of Columbia College.

delegates.name: Rufus King
delegates.notable_role: Active debater on slavery and commerce; later U.S. senator and minister to Britain. 'Life and Correspondence of Rufus King' (6 vols, ed. C.R. King) is a major source.

delegates.name: John Langdon
delegates.notable_role: Funded the New Hampshire delegation out of his own pocket; later first president pro tempore of the U.S. Senate.

delegates.name: John Lansing Jr.
delegates.notable_role: Walked out with Yates on July 10, opposed to the entire Convention plan; later led NY Anti-Federalist forces.

delegates.name: William Livingston
delegates.notable_role: Sitting Governor of New Jersey during the Convention; chaired the slave-trade compromise committee.

delegates.name: James Madison
delegates.notable_role: Principal architect of the Virginia Plan and the most complete note-taker of the proceedings. Co-author of The Federalist; introduced the Bill of Rights in the First Congress; 4th President.

delegates.name: Alexander Martin
delegates.notable_role: Former and future Governor of North Carolina; left the Convention without explanation in late August.

delegates.name: Luther Martin
delegates.notable_role: Walked out in protest; published 'The Genuine Information' (1788), one of the most thorough Anti-Federalist accounts of the Convention's secret debates.

delegates.name: George Mason
delegates.notable_role: Author of the Virginia Declaration of Rights (1776). Refused to sign over the absence of a bill of rights; his 'Objections' (1787) was the founding Anti-Federalist text.

delegates.name: James McClurg
delegates.notable_role: Replaced Patrick Henry, who refused to attend. Left in early August with little record of speeches.

delegates.name: James McHenry
delegates.notable_role: Kept private notes of the Convention complementary to Madison's; later Secretary of War (1796–1800). Fort McHenry namesake.

delegates.name: John Francis Mercer
delegates.notable_role: Outspoken Anti-Federalist; left after a few weeks. Later Governor of Maryland.

delegates.name: Thomas Mifflin
delegates.notable_role: Continental Army general; later first Governor of Pennsylvania under the new state constitution.

delegates.name: Gouverneur Morris
delegates.notable_role: Author of the polished final text — including the Preamble's 'We the People of the United States'. Spoke 173 times, more than any other delegate.

delegates.name: Robert Morris
delegates.notable_role: Continental Superintendent of Finance during the Revolution; nominated Washington for Convention president. Later first U.S. senator from Pennsylvania.

delegates.name: William Paterson
delegates.notable_role: Authored the New Jersey Plan defending equal-state representation; later Governor of New Jersey and Justice of the U.S. Supreme Court.

delegates.name: William Pierce
delegates.notable_role: Wrote 'Character Sketches of the Delegates to the Federal Convention' — the most cited contemporary description of the men in the room.

delegates.name: Charles Pinckney
delegates.notable_role: Submitted his own 'Pinckney Plan' on May 29; speech of October 1787 published as 'Observations on the Plan of Government' is a major Federalist document.

delegates.name: Charles Cotesworth Pinckney
delegates.notable_role: Negotiated the slave-trade compromise; later twice Federalist nominee for President.

delegates.name: Edmund Randolph
delegates.notable_role: Introduced the Virginia Plan on May 29; refused to sign in September but reversed and supported ratification at the Virginia convention. First U.S. Attorney General.

delegates.name: George Read
delegates.notable_role: Signed for John Dickinson by proxy; later U.S. senator and Chief Justice of Delaware.

delegates.name: John Rutledge
delegates.notable_role: Chair of the Committee of Detail that produced the working draft. Later second Chief Justice of the United States (recess appointment).

delegates.name: Roger Sherman
delegates.notable_role: Co-author of the Connecticut Compromise. Only person to sign the Articles of Association, the Declaration of Independence, the Articles of Confederation, AND the Constitution.

delegates.name: Richard Dobbs Spaight
delegates.notable_role: Later Governor of North Carolina; killed in an 1802 duel.

delegates.name: Caleb Strong
delegates.notable_role: Left before signing because of family illness; later led Massachusetts ratification and was elected Governor seven times.

delegates.name: George Washington
delegates.notable_role: Unanimously elected president of the Convention; spoke once on substance. Later first President of the United States.

delegates.name: Hugh Williamson
delegates.notable_role: Physician-scientist; spoke frequently on commerce and slavery. Wrote 'Remarks on the New Plan of Government' (1788).

delegates.name: James Wilson
delegates.notable_role: Member of the Committee of Detail; second-most-frequent speaker after G. Morris. Read Franklin's closing speech. Original U.S. Supreme Court Justice. Author of 'Lectures on Law' (1790–91), one of the founding theoretical statements of American constitutionalism.

delegates.name: George Wythe
delegates.notable_role: Foremost legal scholar among the delegates; left in early June because of his wife's illness. Author of 'Decisions of Cases in Virginia' (1795).

delegates.name: Robert Yates
delegates.notable_role: Walked out with Lansing on July 10. His 'Secret Proceedings and Debates of the Convention' (published posthumously, 1821) is the second major contemporary source after Madison's notes; widely believed to be the author of the 'Brutus' Anti-Federalist essays.
